script.hook: How did one volcano darken summers across the world?
script.title: The Eruption That Stole a Summer
script.narration: How did one volcano darken summers across the world? In April eighteen fifteen, Mount Tambora erupted in Indonesia, hurling ash and sulfur gases high into the atmosphere. As the sulfur gases spread, they formed tiny particles that reflected some sunlight back into space. With less solar energy reaching the surface, global temperatures dipped, but the effects varied by place and weather. The following year, parts of Europe and North America endured cold, wet conditions during the season when crops needed warmth. Harvests failed, food grew scarce, and summer felt as if it had vanished beneath clouds and rain. Tambora didn’t remove an ocean; its eruption sent a chain of consequences across the world, until distant communities felt the chill of a volcano they’d never seen.

voiceover.narration_script: How did one volcano darken summers across the world? In April eighteen fifteen, Mount Tambora erupted in Indonesia, hurling ash and sulfur gases high into the atmosphere. As the sulfur gases spread, they formed tiny particles that reflected some sunlight back into space. With less solar energy reaching the surface, global temperatures dipped, but the effects varied by place and weather. The following year, parts of Europe and North America endured cold, wet conditions during the season when crops needed warmth. Harvests failed, food grew scarce, and summer felt as if it had vanished beneath clouds and rain. Tambora didn’t remove an ocean; its eruption sent a chain of consequences across the world, until distant communities felt the chill of a volcano they’d never seen.
